symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of independently sampled units.

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: The H\"older order of the single observed-outcome regression \(\mu_P\), with \(q\geq1\).

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: A fixed envelope for compact support, score density, regression H\"older norm, and conditional variance in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\).

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: The observed location covariate whose support boundary indexes the regression target.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: A member law for the observed outcome and bivariate random-design covariate.

symbols.name: \widehat{\mu}_n
symbols.def: A generic CTY rule whose value at \(x\) is a measurable function of \(V_{n,P}(x)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{NP}}_n
symbols.def: The inherited CTY decision class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:cty\text{-}distance\text{-}decision\text{-}class}\).

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{NP}}
definitions.construction:
\[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)=\bigl\{P:\text{conditions (i)--(iv) below hold}\bigr\}.\]
Condition \(\mathrm{(i)}\): for every \(n\), \((Y_i,X_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independently and identically distributed under \(P\) in \(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2\).  Condition \(\mathrm{(ii)}\): \(X\) has a Lebesgue density \(f_P\), continuous on its compact support \(\mathcal X_P\subseteq[-L,L]^2\), with \(L^{-1}\leq\inf_{x\in\mathcal X_P}f_P(x)\leq\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_P}f_P(x)\leq L\), and \(\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\) is a rectifiable curve.  Condition \(\mathrm{(iii)}\): \(\mu_P(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=x]\) belongs to \(\mathcal H^q(\mathcal X_P,L)\).  Condition \(\mathrm{(iv)}\): \(\sigma_P^2(x)=\operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid X=x)\) is continuous on \(\mathcal X_P\) and satisfies \(L^{-1}\leq\sigma_P^2(x)\leq L\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X_P\).

definitions.name: \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{NP}}_n
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}=\left\{\widehat\mu_n:\widehat\mu_n(x)=T_{n,x}(V_{n,P}(x))\text{ for a measurable }T_{n,x}\text{ selected independently of }P\text{ at every }x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\right\}.\]

statements.statement:
Let all spaces carrying \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M,S_1,\ldots,S_M\) be standard Borel.  Let \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\) be independent uniform binary variables.  Conditionally on them, let \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) be independent, with the law of \(Z_j\) depending only on \(\Omega_j\) for \(1\leq j\leq M\), and with the law of \(Z_0\) independent of \((\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M)\).  Suppose decoder \(j\) is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\), where \(S_j\) is a measurable compression of \(Z_j\), and write \(Q_{j,b}=\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=b)\) and \(\rho_j=1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Then every such decentralized decoder obeys
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]
In particular, if \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq\kappa\log M\) for all \(j\) and a fixed \(\kappa<1\), then the probability of at least one decoding error is at least \(1/2-o(1)\).
statements.proof_tex:
For each \(j\), dominate \(Q_{j,0}\) and \(Q_{j,1}\) by \(Q_{j,0}+Q_{j,1}\), and write the resulting densities as \(q_{j,0}\) and \(q_{j,1}\).  The common subprobability measure has density \(q_{j,0}\wedge q_{j,1}\) and mass
\[
 \rho_j=\int(q_{j,0}\wedge q_{j,1})
 =1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
Construct the following equivalent version of the experiment.  Independently across coordinates, draw an ambiguity indicator \(A_j\), independent of \(\Omega_j\), with \(\Pr(A_j=1)=\rho_j\).  On \(\{A_j=1\}\), draw \(S_j\) from the normalized common submeasure, independently of \(\Omega_j\).  On \(\{A_j=0\}\), draw it from the normalized residual measure belonging to \(\Omega_j\).  A residual of mass zero may be assigned any probability kernel, because its associated event has probability zero.  This mixture has conditional law \(Q_{j,b}\) when \(\Omega_j=b\).

Because all spaces are standard Borel, a regular conditional distribution of \(Z_j\) given \((S_j,\Omega_j)\) exists.  Drawing from these conditional distributions reconstructs the prescribed conditional law of every \(Z_j\); drawing \(Z_0\) independently from its bit-independent law reconstructs the joint experiment by the assumed conditional product structure.

Condition on the ambiguity indicators and on all randomization other than the bits, and also condition on all bits outside
\[
 \mathcal A=\{j:A_j=1\}.
\]
If \(\mathcal A\neq\varnothing\), regard simultaneous success as a subset of the configurations of the remaining bits.  Two configurations differing only in coordinate \(j\in\mathcal A\) cannot both be successful: decoder \(j\) then receives the same \(S_j\), the same \(Z_{-j}\), and the same \(Z_0\), while the correct value of \(\Omega_j\) is reversed.  The successful configurations therefore form an independent set in the \(|\mathcal A|\)-dimensional binary hypercube.  Pairing vertices along any one coordinate shows that this set has at most \(2^{|\mathcal A|-1}\) elements.  Conditional on the fixed objects, the ambiguous bits remain independent and uniform.  Hence the conditional probability of simultaneous success is at most \(1/2\) when \(\mathcal A\neq\varnothing\), and is at most one when \(\mathcal A=\varnothing\).  Averaging gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 &\leq \Pr(\mathcal A=\varnothing)+\frac12\Pr(\mathcal A\neq\varnothing)\\
 &=\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

For the relative-entropy consequence, let
\[
 H_j=\int\sqrt{q_{j,0}q_{j,1}}
\]
be the Hellinger affinity.  Jensen's inequality under \(Q_{j,0}\), followed by the standard affinity bound for total variation, gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\geq-2\log H_j,
 \qquad
 \lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq\sqrt{1-H_j^2}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \rho_j
 \geq1-\sqrt{1-e^{-\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})}}
 \geq\frac12e^{-\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})}.
\]
If \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq\kappa\log M\), then
\[
 \rho_j\geq\frac12M^{-\kappa},
 \qquad
 \prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)
 \leq\exp\{-M^{1-\kappa}/2\}=o(1),
\]
because \(\kappa<1\).  Substitution in the first conclusion proves that the probability of at least one decoding error is at least \(1/2-o(1)\).

statements.statement:
For every \(q\geq1\) and \(L\geq4\), there are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1/8\), depending only on \(q\) and \(L\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), there exist \(M_n\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}\) points \(x_1,\ldots,x_{M_n}\) on the boundary of the square \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\), separated by at least a constant multiple of \(a_n^{1/q}\), and laws \(P_\omega\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\), indexed by \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^{M_n}\), with the following properties.  Every law has support \(S\), a continuous density \(f_{P_\omega}\) satisfying \(L^{-1}\leq f_{P_\omega}\leq L\), a regression \(\mu_{P_\omega}\) in the stated \(q\)-H\"older ball, and a continuous conditional variance \(\sigma^2_{P_\omega}\) satisfying \(L^{-1}\leq\sigma^2_{P_\omega}\leq L\).  The boundary \(\operatorname{bd}(S)\) is rectifiable and the observations are independently and identically distributed.  If \(\omega^{(j)}\) differs from \(\omega\) only in coordinate \(j\), then
\[
 \left|\mu_{P_\omega}(x_j)-\mu_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)\right|\geq c_1a_n,
\]
the laws of \(\lVert X-x_j\rVert_2\) agree, the conditional radial outcome laws agree outside radii of order \(a_n\), and
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_\omega}\{V_{n,P_\omega}(x_j)\},
 \mathcal L_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}\{V_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)\}\right)
 \leq\alpha\log M_n.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\), and place all centers on a fixed middle subinterval of the lower edge of \(S\).  If \(x_j\) is such a center, then for every sufficiently small \(r>0\) the part of the circle of radius \(r\) lying in \(S\) is
\[
 x_j+r e_\theta,
 \qquad e_\theta=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta),
 \qquad 0\leq\theta\leq\pi.
\]
The construction uses the identities
\[
 \int_0^\pi\cos\theta\,d\theta=0,
 \qquad
 \int_0^\pi\cos^2\theta\,d\theta=\frac\pi2.
\]

Choose \(\psi\in C_c^\infty((-1,1))\) with \(0\leq\psi\leq1\) and \(\psi(0)=1\), and set
\[
 \phi(z)=\psi(\lVert z\rVert_2^2),
 \qquad
 \varphi(u)=\psi(u^2).
\]
For constants \(d,d_1>0\), to be chosen below, define
\[
 \Delta=d a_n,
 \qquad
 w=(d_1\Delta)^{1/q}.
\]
Choose a maximal grid of centers on the indicated middle subinterval with separation \(3w\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), the half-discs \(C_j=B_2(x_j,w)\cap S\) are pairwise disjoint and avoid the corners.  Elementary interval packing gives
\[
 M_n\asymp w^{-1},
 \qquad
 M_n\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q},
\]
where all constants may depend on \(q\) and \(L\).  In particular, the separation is a constant multiple of \(a_n^{1/q}\).  Write \(r_j(z)=\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2\) and \(\phi_j(z)=\phi((z-x_j)/w)\).

Fix a sufficiently small slope \(b>0\).  For \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^{M_n}\), define
\[
 p_\omega(z)=\frac12+bz_1+Delta\sum_{j=1}^{M_n}\omega_j\phi_j(z).
\]
For every integer \(0\leq k\leq q\), scaling gives
\[
 \lVert D^k(\Delta\phi_j)\rVert_\infty
 \leq C_{\phi,q}\Delta w^{-k}.
\]
For \(k=q\), the right-hand side is \(C_{\phi,q}/d_1\); for \(k<q\), it converges to zero.  The supports are disjoint, so summation does not enlarge these suprema.  Choose \(b\) small, next \(d_1\) large, and finally \(d\) small.  The affine part and scaled bumps then put every \(p_\omega\) in \(\mathcal H^q(S,L)\), and, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \frac14\leq p_\omega(z)\leq\frac34.
\]

Let \(\chi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)\) satisfy \(0\leq\chi\leq1\), \(\chi(v)=0\) for \(v\leq1\), and \(\chi(v)=1\) for \(v\geq2\).  Fix \(c_A\geq8\), increasing \(d_1\) if necessary so that \(2c_A\Delta/b<w\) eventually also when \(q=1\), and define
\[
 A_n(r)=-\frac{2\Delta\varphi(r/w)}{br}
 \chi\!\left(\frac{br}{c_A\Delta}\right),
 \qquad A_n(0)=0.
\]
The cutoff makes \(A_n\) identically zero in a neighborhood of zero, while compact support of \(\varphi(r/w)\) makes it vanish smoothly before \(r=w\).  On the region where it can be nonzero, \(br>c_A\Delta\), and hence
\[
 |A_n(r)|\leq\frac{2}{c_A}\leq\frac14.
\]
Define on \(S\)
\[
 f_\omega(z)=1+
 \sum_{j=1}^{M_n}\omega_j A_n(r_j(z))
 \frac{z_1-(x_j)_1}{r_j(z)}\mathbf1\{r_j(z)<w\},
\]
with each summand defined to be zero at its center.  Disjointness makes the formula unambiguous.  The two cutoff properties show that \(f_\omega\) is continuous on \(S\), and
\[
 \frac34\leq f_\omega(z)\leq\frac54.
\]
For each affected half-disc, polar integration gives
\[
 \int_0^w A_n(r)r\,dr\int_0^\pi\cos\theta\,d\theta=0.
\]
Therefore \(\int_S f_\omega(z)\,dz=1\).  Positivity makes \(S\) the support.  Since \(L\geq4\), the displayed density interval is contained in \([L^{-1},L]\), and \(S\subset[-L,L]^2\) is compact with rectifiable boundary.

Conditional on \(X=z\), let
\[
 Y=B+\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 B\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_\omega(z)),
 \qquad
 \varepsilon\sim N(0,1),
\]
where \(B\) and \(\varepsilon\) are conditionally independent.  Then
\[
 \mu_{P_\omega}(z)=p_\omega(z),
 \qquad
 \sigma_{P_\omega}^2(z)=1+p_\omega(z)\{1-p_\omega(z)\}.
\]
The variance is continuous and belongs to \([1,5/4]\subseteq[L^{-1},L]\).  Draw the \(n\) observations independently from this common law.  Thus condition \(\mathrm{(i)}\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) holds by construction; condition \(\mathrm{(ii)}\) follows from compactness, rectifiability, normalization, continuity, positivity, and the density envelope just verified; condition \(\mathrm{(iii)}\) is the scaled H\"older calculation; and condition \(\mathrm{(iv)}\) is the displayed variance calculation.  Hence every \(P_\omega\) belongs to the same class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\).

It remains to establish the compressed-experiment properties.  Compare adjacent vertices, orienting the notation first so that \(\omega_j=1\) and \(\omega_j^{(j)}=0\).  All other perturbations vanish in \(C_j\).  At every \(0<r<w\), the angular density correction has integral zero, so the two radial densities agree and equal \(\pi r\).  For \(r\geq w\), the adjacent score densities are pointwise identical.  Thus the complete laws of \(\lVert X-x_j\rVert_2\) agree.

For \(0<r<w\), the difference of the outcome-weighted angular integrals is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\int_0^\pi p_\omega(x_j+re_\theta)
 \{1+A_n(r)\cos\theta\}\,d\theta
 -\int_0^\pi p_{\omega^{(j)}}(x_j+re_\theta)\,d\theta\\
 &\qquad=\pi\Delta\varphi(r/w)+\frac\pi2brA_n(r).
\end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, the constant part and the radial bump multiplied by \(A_n(r)\cos\theta\) integrate to zero, while the affine angular term gives the second cosine identity above.  If \(br\geq2c_A\Delta\), then \(\chi=1\) and the last display is zero.  For \(r\geq w\), both perturbations vanish.  Conditional on a radius, an angular mixture of Bernoulli variables is Bernoulli with the angularly averaged success probability, and convolution with the common Gaussian preserves equality.  Therefore the conditional radial outcome laws agree outside
\[
 0\leq r<\frac{2c_A\Delta}{b},
\]
an interval whose length is of order \(a_n\).

On this exceptional interval the common radial density is bounded by \(Cr\), both averaged Bernoulli probabilities lie in \([1/4,3/4]\), and their difference is at most \(C\Delta\).  For such probabilities,
\[
 \operatorname{kl}(p,p')
 \leq\frac{(p-p')^2}{p'(1-p')}
 \leq C\Delta^2.
\]
Adding the common Gaussian is a Markov kernel, so relative entropy cannot increase.  Disintegration with respect to the common radial marginal consequently gives, for one compressed observation,
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P^{\mathrm{rad}}_{\omega,j},P^{\mathrm{rad}}_{\omega^{(j)},j})
 \leq C\Delta^2\int_0^{2c_A\Delta/b}r\,dr
 \leq C'\Delta^4.
\]
This argument is unchanged after reversing the adjacent orientation.  Independent-product tensorization now yields
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_{P_\omega}\{V_{n,P_\omega}(x_j)\},
 \mathcal L_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}\{V_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)\}
 \right)
 \leq C'n\Delta^4=C'd^4\log n.
\]
Because the chosen maximal grid has \(M_n\asymp w^{-1}\),
\[
 \log M_n=\left(\frac{1}{4q}+o(1)\right)\log n.
\]
Choose \(d>0\) small enough that the preceding divergence is at most \(\alpha\log M_n\) for one fixed \(0<\alpha<1/8\), without disturbing any earlier envelope choice.  Finally, \(\phi_j(x_j)=1\), while the other bumps vanish at \(x_j\), and hence
\[
 |\mu_{P_\omega}(x_j)-\mu_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)|
 =\Delta=d a_n.
\]
Taking \(c_1=d\) completes the construction and proves every assertion.

Fix \(q\geq 1\) and \(L\geq 4\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), take the explicit family supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:cty\text{-}support\text{-}boundary\text{-}angular\text{-}packing}\).  Write \(M=M_n\), \(\Delta=c_1a_n\), and let \(C_j=B_2(x_j,w)\cap S\) be the disjoint half-disc cells used in that construction.  At \(x_j\), the value \(\mu_{P_\omega}(x_j)\) depends only on \(\omega_j\), and its two possible values are separated by \(\Delta\).

Let \(\widehat\mu_n\in\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\) be arbitrary.  We first turn it into a rule in an experiment having independent cell restrictions.  Under \(P_\omega\), generate a Poisson point process of mean \(2n\) on the observation space and attach independent marks with a continuous distribution.  If its point count \(N\) is at least \(n\), retain the \(n\) observations with the smallest marks, in increasing-mark order, and apply \(\widehat\mu_n\); if \(N<n\), return the zero boundary function.  Denote the resulting rule by \(\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{Pois}}\).  Conditional on every value \(N=k\geq n\), the retained observations are an independent sample from \(P_\omega\): the marks are independent of the observations, and their ordering induces a random permutation independent of the observation values.  This construction is independent of \(\omega\) and of \(P_\omega\).

Place independent uniform bits \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\) on the packing vertices.  Let \(Z_j\) be the complete marked restriction of the Poisson process to \(C_j\), and let \(Z_0\) be its restriction to the complement of the union of the cells.  Conditional on the bits, the variables \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) are independent by the independent-restrictions property of a Poisson process.  The explicit packing has the further properties that the law of \(Z_j\) depends only on \(\Omega_j\), whereas the law of \(Z_0\) is bit-independent.  Let \(S_j\) retain from \(Z_j\) only each point's mark, outcome, and distance from \(x_j\).  At \(x_j\), the coordinatewise rule \(\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{Pois}}\) is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\): the full restrictions outside \(C_j\) reveal their distances from \(x_j\), and \(S_j\) supplies exactly the information about points inside \(C_j\) permitted by \(V_{n,P_\omega}(x_j)\).

We next verify the divergence hypothesis for this marked cell experiment.  In the packing construction, adjacent laws are identical off \(C_j\), the mass of \(C_j\) is the same under the two adjacent laws, and every point at distance less than \(w\) from \(x_j\) belongs to \(C_j\).  Thus the one-observation radial law is a common component outside \(C_j\) plus the local compressed component, with disjoint radial supports up to null boundaries.  If \(D_j\) denotes the relative entropy between the two one-observation local compressed components, tensorization and the packing lemma give
\[
 nD_j
 =\operatorname{KL}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_{P_\omega}\{V_{n,P_\omega}(x_j)\},
 \mathcal L_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}\{V_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)\}
 \right)
 \leq \alpha\log M.
\]
Independent marks add zero relative entropy.  The relative-entropy formula for Poisson point processes with equal finite component masses therefore yields, for \(Q_{j,b}=\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=b)\),
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})=2nD_j\leq 2\alpha\log M.
\]
The same bound holds in the reverse orientation.  Since \(2\alpha<1\), \(\mathrm{lem:coordinatewise\text{-}overlap\text{-}direct\text{-}product}\), with \(\kappa=2\alpha\), is applicable.

At each \(x_j\), decode \(\Omega_j\) by thresholding \(\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{Pois}}(x_j)\) at the midpoint of the two possible regression values.  The direct-product lemma and \(M_n\to\infty\) imply
\[
 \Pr\{\text{at least one coordinate is decoded incorrectly}\}
 \geq \frac12-o(1).
\]
If the uniform boundary loss were less than \(\Delta/2\), every midpoint decoder would be correct.  Averaging first over the uniform bit prior and then using that a maximum dominates an average gives
\[
 \sup_{\omega}
 \mathbb E_{P_\omega}^{\mathrm{Pois}}\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(S)}
 |\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{Pois}}(x)-\mu_{P_\omega}(x)|
 \right]
 \geq \frac{\Delta}{2}\left\{\frac12-o(1)\right\}
 \geq c a_n
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), where \(c>0\) depends only on \(q\) and \(L\).

It remains to de-Poissonize.  Every packing regression takes values in \([1/4,3/4]\), so the loss of the zero default on \(\{N<n\}\) is at most one.  On \(\{N\geq n\}\), the selected data have law \(P_\omega^{\otimes n}\).  Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_\omega
 \mathbb E_{P_\omega}^{\mathrm{Pois}}\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(S)}
 |\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{Pois}}(x)-\mu_{P_\omega}(x)|
 \right]\\
 &\qquad\leq
 \sup_\omega
 \mathbb E_{P_\omega}\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(S)}
 |\widehat\mu_n(x)-\mu_{P_\omega}(x)|
 \right]
 +\Pr\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The exponential Markov inequality gives, for example,
\[
 \Pr\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}
 \leq \exp\{-n(1-\log 2)\}=o(a_n).
\]
Combining the last three displays and decreasing \(c\) if necessary proves, uniformly over the arbitrary rule \(\widehat\mu_n\),
\[
 \sup_\omega
 \mathbb E_{P_\omega}\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(S)}
 |\widehat\mu_n(x)-\mu_{P_\omega}(x)|
 \right]
 \geq c a_n.
\]

The packing lemma verifies all boundary, support, density-positivity, H\"older, variance, and independent-sampling conditions required for \(P_\omega\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\).  Hence the supremum over the full class is no smaller than the supremum over this finite family.  Taking the infimum over the law-independent class \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\) gives
\[
 R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\geq c a_n
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Finally, \(a_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\), while \(\mathrm{def:cty\text{-}distance\text{-}risk}\) identifies the expanded infimum--supremum display with \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\).  Dividing by \(a_n\) and taking lower limits proves the claimed result with \(c_{\mathrm{CTY}}=c\).  The entire finite family lies in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\), so this is a same-class converse and uses no treatment-effect or two-sided-thickness subclass.

sampling_model.design: A boundary discontinuity design with a known binary assignment partition of a compact bivariate score support.
sampling_model.overlap: Each arm has probability mass at least \(c_{-}r^2\) in every boundary ball of radius \(r\) for \(0<r\leq r_0\); \(f_P\leq L\) yields the derived upper estimate \(\pi Lr^2\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The score density is bounded and continuous but has no class-uniform derivative or continuity modulus. Exact-distance regressions use the canonical coarea ratio on positive-denominator radii and the H\"older regression representative on zero-denominator radii. Both distance upper bounds use the fixed triangular kernel and degree zero; the comparison experiment permits estimators to use full score locations jointly.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem~6 gives the \(n^{-1/4}\) lower rate on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\), and the discussion at printed line~551 conjectures that the uniform penalty \(\log^{1/4}n\) is unavoidable.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The retained support-boundary angular packing lies in that same \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) and proves the sharper lower rate \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\); paired with the published uniform upper bound, this gives the exact frontier.

tldr: The coordinatewise distance experiment has a sharp first-order uniform frontier even when the assignment boundary and outcome regressions are arbitrarily smooth. On the primitive rectifiable class with an inspectable arm-specific two-sided design-thickness condition, \(R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}})\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/4}\). The same rate holds on the endpoint-trimmed smooth class because bounded continuous score densities have no common angular regularity modulus; a straight-boundary angular-density packing with affine regressions supplies the converse. On the identical straight geometry, full score locations recover \((\log n/n)^{q/(2q+2)}\), strictly faster for \(q>1\). A central open question asks which primitive density or angular-balance regularity produces a transition to a faster distance-only frontier.

project_justification.gap: Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 6, gives an \(n^{-1/4}\) pointwise-style lower bound over its stated nonparametric class, while the following discussion predicts that uniform estimation carries a logarithmic factor. Their Theorem 3(ii) is a fixed-law interior smooth-bias result and does not determine a class-uniform minimax rate when continuous score densities have no common modulus.
project_justification.niche: The coordinatewise distance release discards angular locations. A primitive two-sided design-thickness condition stabilizes local estimation and supplies separated boundary neighborhoods, while unrestricted shrinking-scale angular imbalance can keep the induced radial regression only first-order regular even on a straight boundary.
project_justification.fill: The rectifiable theorem establishes the predicted logarithmic phenomenon on its own transparent primitive class. The smooth saturation theorem shows that geometry alone does not improve that frontier, and the straight-class comparison isolates the lost information by proving the faster Stone exponent for the full-location experiment.

technical_internal_limitation: The decision restriction is coordinatewise: \(\widehat{\tau}_n(x)\) may use \(U_{n,P}(x)\) but may not triangulate score locations from distances released at other boundary points. A joint multi-center release is a different experiment. Exact-radius conditionals are only determined almost everywhere: the canonical representative uses the coarea ratio where \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\) and the existing H\"older representative \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\) otherwise. Two-sided thickness ensures only that positive-denominator radii accumulate at zero; it does not imply positivity at every radius. The angular-density packing must explicitly construct bounded continuous density perturbations whose imbalance varies at scale \(a_n\), verify common density, tail, variance, H\"older, assignment-partition, reach, and arm-mass constants, keep the straight geometry and affine regressions, and prove the stated compressed-law Kullback--Leibler and packing bounds. Rough density by itself is not a lower-bound proof. For fixed \(P\), the higher-order angular integrals in Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 3(ii), may be differentiable; the diagnostic point is only that no uniform derivative bound follows from this proposal's density envelope. The primitive class here and the anchor's nonparametric class are distinct, and no inclusion is asserted.
honest_scope: The theorem-level targets are rate equivalences, not exact asymptotic constants. Exact-distance conditional expectations are identified only up to null radial sets; the canonical coarea representative fills those radii with \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\), and H\"older continuity makes its boundary limit unique without assuming a positive circle denominator at every radius. The rectifiable result establishes the predicted logarithmic phenomenon only under the novel primitive two-sided design-thickness condition; the logarithmic frontier on the exact nonparametric class of Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 6, remains open. The smooth theorem concerns the fixed endpoint-trimmed target and uses no density modulus beyond continuity and fixed upper and lower bounds. Its lower bound has an explicit compressed-experiment construction obligation on a straight two-half-plane submodel with affine regressions. The full-location Stone exponent is stated only for the separately defined full-location decision class and is strictly faster than the distance exponent only when \(q>1\). The weakest empirically meaningful regularity producing a faster distance-only frontier is open.
